sentences.text: Rayososaurus is considered a medium-sized sauropod with an estimated body mass of 9,353 kg.
Other estimates suggest the animal reached 12 meters in length, 4 meters in height, and weighed 3 tons.
This dinosaur possessed a distinctive racquet-shaped scapula, a feature shared with other rebbachisaurids.
The genus Rayososaurus was named by the Argentinian paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1996.
The genus name honors the Rayoso Formation, which Bonaparte originally believed the fossil came from.
The species name agrioensis refers to the Agrio River near the fossil discovery site.
Later research in 2008 and 2009 determined the specimen actually came from the Candeleros Formation rather than the Rayoso Formation.
In 1998, Jeffrey Wilson and Paul Sereno proposed that the species Rebbachisaurus tessonei should be assigned to the genus Rayososaurus.
The time range for Rayososaurus is also cited as the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
Calvo and Salgado consider Rayososaurus to be a nomen dubium, or doubtful name.
Bonaparte defends the validity of Rayososaurus as the most basal member of the family Rebbachisauridae, citing the typical racquet-shaped scapula.
There is an ongoing debate regarding whether Rayososaurus is a distinct genus given its extreme similarity to Rebbachisaurus.
